First of all, this is a direct sequel to Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc, so play that one first.

Danganronpa 2 fixed a few of my issues from the first game. Unfortunately there's still some logic leaps (not unexpected) but statements you're meant to agree with and statements you're meant to dispute are clearly separated in this entry, which is excellent. The music is fantastic once again, and the characters are pretty good. The minigames are still a little wacky and I still think that the game should not limit the evidence you can present, even with the logic difficulty on the highest setting it still felt a little too simple.

I saw another review that says the first 75% of the game feels like a slog, and it's pretty true. I was still pretty captivated and interested in when Danganronpa 1 would come into play, which kept me going through the first 3 chapters. From chapter 4 onward though, things get insane.

Good game, play the first one if you haven't already.

I had originally only watched the Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc anime adaptation, so I went into Danganronpa 2 expecting a similar story with a mild visual novel presentation. In the end, I was blown away by the quality of the game and how it puts you in control of solving the mystery. The great characters pulled me into a world and story which it was easy to care about, and this helped motivate me when solving the various murders. Loved the character art this time around, the general variety, the cinematics, and the setting. Playing in Japanese, each voice was distinct and memorable, and the tricks employed were unbelievably well-done; especially in comparison to the first game. Characters died appropriately, and killers were appropriately well-developed.

The music followed up well on the animation and what I had been exposed to from the previous themes, and the strong use of pastel character added a finessed style to the whole experience. Trials were challenging and creative, though there was no method of losing out when collecting evidence in the form of "truth bullets." The variety of minigames kept my attention when the story would drag, and I was living for the next chance to investigate and dig out the murderer. Sold me 100% on purchasing Danganronpa V3, and solidified my choice to recommend this game to anyone who even casually enjoys visual novels.

Going to start by making 3 points very clear:
1) This may be the darkest game (thematically) that I have ever played
2) The "Overwhelmingly positive" score is absolutely deserved
3) You really should play the first game before this!

So Danganronpa 2 follows a similar style to the original in that kids are forced to kill each other to survive. After each kill there is a "Class trial" with 2 possible outcomes:
1) You find the killer and they are executed
2) You do not find the killer, the killer can go home, and everyone else is executed

I won't say too much as the story has so many twists and turns that spoilers are far too easy to casually hand out - but this one had my jaw drop on several occasions - especially in the act 5 trial!! The story and, importantly, the localisation is absolutely fantastic!

Both games are on sale at the time that I write this, you really do owe it to yourself to give both a try. DO NOT be put off by the visual novel connections... I am not a fan of that genre, but these two games have had me absolutely hooked throughout!

It's like Ace Attorney meets Saw.

If you are not a visual novels/ dating sims fan like me, I would suggest watching the anime that covers the first game before playing so you can warm up to the story. It's what I did.

PROS
+ Writing.. is TOP. Minimum plot holes, respect to causality and player's intelligence, etc. That helps with immersion for a detective game a lot. It keeps you guessing/on edge constantly.
+ That nowadays rare wacky, lively, out of the box anime vibe that's all over the place. Fan service, adult humor, weird characters, you name it.
+ The soundtrack is sublime. It never gets old even though you listen the tracks repeat for so long.
+ Great visual stylistic choices

CONS
The game graphics are like for a 2000's handheld which is expected for the genre I guess.

While I'd like to write out a detailed review of Dangan 2, I'm so damn salty about what a disappointment it is that I can't bring myself to do so.

I will say that for the most part, 2's story and characters are a welcome improvement on the first game's, at least until the end. But there's still plenty of forgettable and just plain terrible characters. Some minigames are slightly improved while new ones have their own share of annoyances. The murder mysteries as usual are the highlight of the game and really the only reason it's worth playing.

Dangan 2 is basically Dangan 1 with more unnecessary fan service, more cringey "humor" and sexual dialogue, more insufferable characters, and more plot holes than ever. SO. MANY. PLOT HOLES!

Did you like Dangan 1? Do you like when characters conveniently ignore established rules? Do you like cliche, flowery, and repetitive dialogue where everyone comes together with the power of friendship in the end? Do you like being blue-balled by red herring bait after having false mystery built up the entire game? Then Dangan 2 is the game for you!

It baffles me that this series has such a cult following.
